questions.stem: Identical twins share the same DNA, yet one twin who exercises regularly is more muscular than the other. This difference is best explained by:

options.text: A mutation that occurred in one twin after birth
Environmental variation - different lifestyles have produced different phenotypes despite identical genotypes
Genetic variation caused by differences in their chromosomes
One twin inherited different alleles from the father

questions.explanation: Since identical twins have the same genotype, any differences between them must be caused by environmental factors. Exercise is an environmental factor that stimulates muscle growth. This demonstrates that phenotype is determined by both genes AND environment. Muscle mass is an example of a characteristic influenced by both genetic potential and environmental factors.

questions.stem: A student measures the heights of 200 students in her year group and plots the data. The graph shows a smooth bell-shaped curve. What type of variation does height show, and why?

options.text: Discontinuous variation, because students can be classified as short, medium, or tall
Continuous variation, because height is controlled by many genes and environmental factors, producing a range of values
Discontinuous variation, because height is controlled by a single gene with two alleles
Continuous variation, because height is determined entirely by diet

questions.explanation: Height shows continuous variation - it can take any value within a range and shows a normal distribution (bell curve). This is because height is polygenic (controlled by many genes) and also influenced by environmental factors like diet and health. Discontinuous variation (e.g., blood group) has distinct categories with no intermediates.

questions.stem: Blood group in humans (A, B, AB, O) is an example of discontinuous variation. Which statement about discontinuous variation is correct?

options.text: It is entirely controlled by environmental factors
It shows a normal distribution when plotted on a graph
It is controlled by a single gene with distinct categories and no intermediate values
It is influenced by both genes and environment equally

questions.explanation: Discontinuous variation produces distinct categories with no overlap - you are either blood group A, B, AB, or O, with nothing in between. It is typically controlled by a single gene (or very few genes) and is not influenced by the environment. When plotted, the data produces a bar chart rather than a bell curve.

questions.stem: A farmer grows genetically identical wheat plants in two fields: one with rich fertilised soil and one with poor, unfertilised soil. The plants in the rich soil grow taller. What does this demonstrate?

options.text: The plants in rich soil have undergone genetic mutations
Height in wheat is determined entirely by genetics
Environmental factors (soil nutrients) can cause variation in phenotype even when the genotype is identical
The plants in poor soil have different alleles for height

questions.explanation: Since the plants are genetically identical, any difference in height must be due to environmental factors. The plants in nutrient-rich soil had access to more minerals for growth, so they grew taller. This is a clear demonstration that environment affects phenotype. The genotype sets the potential, but the environment determines how much of that potential is realised.

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics is MOST likely to be caused by genetic variation alone with minimal environmental influence?

options.text: Body mass
Skin colour
Blood group
Intelligence

questions.explanation: Blood group is determined entirely by genetics (the ABO gene) and is not affected by the environment. You are born with a blood group and it never changes. Body mass, skin colour, and intelligence are all influenced by both genes and environment (e.g., diet affects body mass, sun exposure affects skin colour, education affects measured intelligence).
